title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults, quantization profiles, unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost and improve out-of-the-box performance for common workloads by making batching and KV-caching defaults adaptive, providing model-appropriate quantization profile recommendations, and surfacing unit-economics signals in the Console and CLI. Changes include: 1) Autotune service that observes per-route latency/throughput and progressively adjusts batching window and cache TTL within SLO-safe bounds; 2) Quantization profile registry and onboarding hooks so model owners get recommended profiles (fp16/4-bit variants) tested against accuracy thresholds; 3) Unit-econ tooling: cost/p95-tokens dashboards, per-route simulation mode, and a CLI command to run batch-simulations against historical traces; 4) Console UX: rollout controls for autotuned params, experiment tracking and regressions alerting tied to eval prompts. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4123) - [x] autotune service + API - [x] quant profiles registry + tests - [x] console + CLI integration - [x] end-to-end e2e + perf benchmarks - [x] docs and migration notes. Related: ENG-4123 (autotune design), ENG-4190 (unit-econ dashboards). Note: this PR combines infra and console changes; rollout is gated behind feature flag 'cost_autotune_v1'.

release_notes: - Autotune service: adaptive batching window and KV-cache TTL autotuning (behind feature flag); - Quantization profiles: model-aware recommendations surfaced in Console; - Unit-econ tooling: new 'redwood cost sim' CLI, Console dashboards for per-route unit economics; - Migration notes: autotune is opt-in and includes a migration script to enable per-route (scripts/migrate_enable_autotune.sh); - No breaking changes expected; rollout gated and monitored.
notes_for_backport: Backport candidates: small config and console wiring can be cherry-picked into release/2026-02 for early customers; autotune core requires runtime dependencies present in main. Coordinate with SRE before backport.
testing_and_benchmarks_summary: E2E tests cover safety bounds, model-version pinning, and quant profile accuracy checks; perf bench against 3 production-like workloads shows 12-28% cost reduction on 8k token tail-heavy routes with median latency unchanged. Bench harness under perf/benchmarks/cost_autotune contains reproducible workloads and scripts.
migration_steps: 1) Run scripts/migrate_enable_autotune.sh in staging to annotate routes (creates feature flag entries); 2) Validate in staging with 'redwood cost sim' against 7-day traces; 3) Enable feature flag for canary orgs and monitor dashboard metrics; 4) Gradual ramp to all orgs if no regressions.
